newsitem.title: UK: OPEC crude output rises to 26.60 mbpd in Dec - IEA.
newsitem.headline: OPEC crude output rises to 26.60 mbpd in Dec - IEA.

text.p: Crude oil production by the Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) rose to 26.60 million barrels per day (bpd) in December from November's 26.14 million bpd, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said in its monthly report on Tuesday.
The figure was well above OPEC's self-assigned by long-ignored production ceiling of 25.03 million bpd.
A 310,000 bpd increase in Iraq to allow for its return to crude exports after a six-year absence accounted for most of the gains, the IEA said.

In its end-December Monthly Oil Market Report, the agency said all but two of the 11 OPEC members appeared to have increased their individual production levels while natural gas liquid output also rose by about 30,000 bpd.
After the implementation in mid-December of the United Nations oil-for-food plan, Iraq increased its average monthly output to 860,000 bpd from 550,000 bod in Novenber, the IEA said.

OPEC heavyweights Saudi Arabia and Iran were both seen by the IEA as over quota. The agency said Saudi Arabia output was 8.26 million bpd compared to its 8.0 million bpd quota while Iranian output was seen at 3.69 million bpd against an OPEC quota of 3.6 million.
It attribuited the Iranian gains of 45,000 bpd over November to refurbishment of offshore platforms damaged in the Iran-Iraq war.

Venezuela, seen by the IEA and many independent monitors as OPEC's biggest quota violator, increased its output in December by 25,000 bpd to 3.05 million bpd. That is well over its 2.36 million quota.
